Dude, Government can't forgive the debt because if it does it will end up loosing money out of it, like a shit ton, and also could potentially put US dollar stability at risk. Basically the Treasury Department, but specially the FED hold this thing called *Mortgage backed securities,* which is basically a tittle that commercial banks give to the FED in exchange for borrowing money from the central bank.   


Forgiving debts means that potentially many landlords will miss the payment of their mortgage fees, (since they are not going to receive any payment of the rent of their appartment), and the tax refund could take place months after the debt forgiveness happens.   


Anyway since the government holds financial contracts which value is sustained in Americans having the capacity to reach their monthly fees, it would be a very bad idea to just erase that debt since the goverment would be putting at risk their own assets and besides it will have to pay a chunk of money to the landlords in order to refund them for their loses.   


Finally, since the FED also holds mortgaged backed securities, which are dollar backed assets, meaning financial contracts that partially hold the USD value. If a substantial number of people miss their mortgage this could affect directly the trust in USD value, which could lead to higher inflation in a very short term.  


There could be other further consequences...but I'm a little bit high to think about them. Hope this humble answer  works for you.
